description: A tiny 8-pin AVR microcontroller with 6 usable GPIO pins (PB0-PB5), no dedicated UART, and no separate USB programmer — it's flashed via an external programmer, not a USB cable.
how_to_use: PB0-PB4 are general-purpose digital I/O, also usable as analog inputs (ADC0-ADC3) and, on PB0/PB1, as PWM outputs. PB5 doubles as the chip's hardware reset line, so it's excluded from the default pool as a plain GPIO pin unless a lesson specifically repurposes it. PB0/PB1/PB2 also carry the chip's single USI peripheral, which is software-configured as either I2C or SPI (never both at once) — not marked as protocol-fixed here since which protocol (if either) applies depends on the sketch, not the hardware alone.

plain.what: A tiny 8-legged chip that is a whole microcontroller — for when an Arduino board is too big for a finished project.
plain.how: You program it using an Arduino as a helper, then it can run on its own with just a battery. Only 5 of its legs are free for your parts.
